title.en: Biographies of Zhang Shizhi and Feng Tang
title.raw: 《張釋之馮唐列傳》 Biographies of Zhang Shizhi and Feng Tang

sentences.zh: 張廷尉釋之者，堵陽人也，字季。

translations.literal: Zhang Shizhi, the Commandant of Justice, was from Duyang and his courtesy name was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi, the Commandant of Justice, was a native of Duyang. His courtesy name was Ji.

sentences.zh: 有兄仲同居。

translations.literal: He had an elder brother Zhong with whom he lived.
translations.idiomatic: He had an elder brother named Zhong, with whom he shared a household.

sentences.zh: 以訾為騎郎，事孝文帝，十歲不得調，無所知名。

translations.literal: He became a mounted attendant through purchase and served Emperor Wen, but for ten years received no promotion and remained unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased a position as a mounted attendant and served Emperor Wen, but for ten years received no promotion and remained entirely unknown.

sentences.zh: 釋之曰：「久宦減仲之產，不遂。」

translations.literal: Shizhi said: "Long service in office diminishes Zhong's property—I cannot succeed this way."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi said: "Long service in office has been depleting Zhong's property—I cannot make a success of this."

sentences.zh: 欲自免歸。

translations.literal: He wished to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to resign his post and return home.

sentences.zh: 中郎將袁盎知其賢，惜其去，乃請徙釋之補謁者。

translations.literal: The Colonel Yuan Ang knew his worth and regretted his departure, so he requested to transfer Shizhi to fill the position of usher.
translations.idiomatic: The Colonel of the Guard Yuan Ang recognized his talent and was reluctant to see him leave, so he petitioned to have Shizhi transferred to fill a vacancy as an usher.

sentences.zh: 釋之既朝畢，因前言便宜事。

translations.literal: After Shizhi finished his court duties, he stepped forward to speak of matters of advantage.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizhi completed his court duties, he stepped forward to speak on matters of practical governance.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「卑之，毋甚高論，令今可施行也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Keep it low—do not discourse too loftily; make it something that can be put into practice now."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "Keep it modest—do not discourse too loftily; speak of what can be put into practice now."

sentences.zh: 於是釋之言秦漢之閒事，秦所以失而漢所以興者久之。

translations.literal: Then Shizhi spoke at length of affairs between Qin and Han, why Qin lost and why Han rose.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi then spoke at length about the transition from Qin to Han—why the Qin fell and why the Han rose.

sentences.zh: 文帝稱善，乃拜釋之為謁者仆射。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised it as good and appointed Shizhi as Chief Usher.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised his discourse and appointed him Chief Usher.

sentences.zh: 釋之從行，登虎圈。

translations.literal: Shizhi accompanied him on a trip and ascended the tiger enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi accompanied the emperor on an excursion and climbed up to the tiger enclosure.

sentences.zh: 上問上林尉諸禽獸簿，十餘問，尉左右視，盡不能對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the Shanglin superintendent about the registers of various birds and beasts, asking more than ten questions, but the superintendent looked left and right and could answer none.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the Shanglin superintendent about the registers of the various birds and beasts, posing more than ten questions. The superintendent looked helplessly about but could not answer a single one.

sentences.zh: 虎圈嗇夫從旁代尉對上所問禽獸簿甚悉，欲以觀其能口對響應無窮者。

translations.literal: The tiger enclosure bailiff from the side replaced the superintendent in answering the emperor's questions about the bird and beast registers very thoroughly, wishing to show his ability for oral response and endless echoes.
translations.idiomatic: The bailiff of the tiger enclosure stepped in from the side to answer the emperor's questions about the animal registers in meticulous detail, eager to display his ability to respond without pause to any query.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「吏不當若是邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Should an official not be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "Should an official not be like this?

sentences.zh: 尉無賴！」

translations.literal: The superintendent is worthless!"
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent is worthless!"

sentences.zh: 乃詔釋之拜嗇夫為上林令。

translations.literal: He then commanded Shizhi to appoint the bailiff as Shanglin magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Shizhi to appoint the bailiff as the Magistrate of Shanglin.

sentences.zh: 釋之久之前曰：「陛下以絳侯周勃何如人也？」

translations.literal: After deliberating at length, Shizhi stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty, what kind of man was the Marquis of Jiang, Zhou Bo?"
translations.idiomatic: After deliberating at length, Shizhi stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty, what kind of man was the Marquis of Jiang, Zhou Bo?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「長者也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A man of worth."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A man of worth."

sentences.zh: 又復問：「東陽侯張相如何如人也？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "What kind of man was the Marquis of Dongyang, Zhang Xiangru?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "What kind of man was the Marquis of Dongyang, Zhang Xiangru?"

sentences.zh: 上復曰：「長者。」

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "A man of worth."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again said: "A man of worth."

sentences.zh: 釋之曰：「夫絳侯、東陽侯稱為長者，此兩人言事曾不能出口，豈斅此嗇夫諜諜利口捷給哉！

translations.literal: Shizhi said: "The Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Dongyang are called men of worth—yet these two, when speaking of affairs, could scarcely get a word out. How could they be like this bailiff with his glib, quick tongue!
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi said: "The Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Dongyang are called men of worth—yet these two, when speaking of affairs, could scarcely get a word out. How could they be like this bailiff with his glib, quick tongue!

sentences.zh: 且秦以任刀筆之吏，吏爭以亟疾苛察相高，然其敝徒文具耳，無惻隱之實。

translations.literal: Moreover, Qin employed officials skilled with brush and knife, officials competed to outdo each other in harsh and hasty scrutiny, yet its defects were merely formal documents, lacking any true compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Qin relied on petty clerks skilled only with brush and blade. These officials vied to outdo one another in harsh scrutiny and hasty judgment, yet the result was nothing but empty paperwork, devoid of any genuine compassion.

sentences.zh: 以故不聞其過，陵遲而至於二世，天下土崩。

translations.literal: Therefore, they did not hear of their faults, gradually declining until the Second Generation, when the empire collapsed like crumbling earth.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the throne never learned of its own failings. The dynasty declined by degrees until the Second Emperor, when the empire crumbled to dust.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以嗇夫口辯而超遷之，臣恐天下隨風靡靡，爭為口辯而無其實。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, because of this bailiff's verbal dexterity, promotes him extraordinarily. I fear all under heaven will follow this wind and drift along, contending to be verbally dexterous while lacking substance.
translations.idiomatic: Now if Your Majesty promotes this bailiff merely for his verbal dexterity, I fear the entire empire will follow the prevailing wind, everyone competing to be glib while neglecting substance.

sentences.zh: 且下之化上疾於景響，舉錯不可不審也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the lower modeling the upper is swifter than an echo following a shadow—Your Majesty's actions cannot but be weighed with care."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people below take their cue from above more swiftly than an echo follows a shadow—Your Majesty's every action must be weighed with utmost care."

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "Good."

sentences.zh: 乃止不拜嗇夫。

translations.literal: He then stopped and did not appoint the bailiff.
translations.idiomatic: He then rescinded the order and did not appoint the bailiff.

sentences.zh: 上就車，召釋之參乘，徐行，問釋之秦之敝。

translations.literal: The emperor boarded the carriage, summoned Shizhi to ride as companion, proceeded slowly, and asked Shizhi about Qin's defects.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted his carriage, summoned Shizhi to ride alongside as a companion, and proceeded slowly, asking Shizhi about the failings of the Qin.

sentences.zh: 具以質言。

translations.literal: He spoke plainly and fully.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi answered plainly and in full.

sentences.zh: 至宮，上拜釋之為公車令。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the palace, the emperor appointed Shizhi as Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the palace, the emperor appointed Shizhi as the Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 頃之，太子與梁王共車入朝，不下司馬門，於是釋之追止太子、梁王無得入殿門。

translations.literal: Soon after, the crown prince and King Liang entered the court together in the same carriage without descending at the Marshal's Gate, so Shizhi pursued and stopped the crown prince and King Liang from entering the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, the Crown Prince and the King of Liang rode together in one carriage to attend court, failing to dismount at the Marshal's Gate. Shizhi gave chase and barred them from entering the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 遂劾不下公門不敬，奏之。

translations.literal: He then impeached them for not descending at the public gate, a sign of disrespect, and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached them for failing to dismount at the palace gate—a breach of protocol—and submitted a formal memorial.

sentences.zh: 薄太后聞之，文帝免冠謝曰：「教兒子不謹。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bo heard of it. Emperor Wen removed his cap and apologized, saying: "I have not taught my sons with sufficient care."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bo heard of it. Emperor Wen removed his cap and apologized, saying: "I have not taught my sons with sufficient care."

sentences.zh: 薄太后乃使使承詔赦太子、梁王，然後得入。

translations.literal: Empress Bo then sent messengers to pardon the crown prince and King Liang according to the imperial command, after which they were allowed to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bo then dispatched messengers bearing an imperial edict to pardon the Crown Prince and the King of Liang, after which they were permitted to enter.

sentences.zh: 文帝由是奇釋之，拜為中大夫。

translations.literal: From this Emperor Wen regarded Shizhi as extraordinary and appointed him Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: From this, Emperor Wen came to regard Shizhi as remarkable and appointed him Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，至中郎將。

translations.literal: Soon after, he reached the rank of Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was promoted to Colonel of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 從行至霸陵，居北臨廁。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor on a visit to Baling, where they took their place on the north side overlooking the tomb passage.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on a visit to the Baling tomb site, where they stood on the northern slope overlooking the steep descent into the burial mound.

sentences.zh: 是時慎夫人從，上指示慎夫人新豐道，曰：「此走邯鄲道也。」

translations.literal: At this time Lady Shen was in attendance. The emperor pointed out the Xinfeng road to Lady Shen and said: "This is the road to Handan."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Lady Shen was in attendance. The emperor pointed out the Xinfeng road to Lady Shen and said: "This is the road to Handan."

sentences.zh: 使慎夫人鼓瑟，上自倚瑟而歌，意慘悽悲懷，顧謂群臣曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: He had Lady Shen play the se; the emperor himself leaned on the se and sang, his mood mournful and full of grief. He turned to the assembled ministers and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: He had Lady Shen play the zither; the emperor himself leaned on the zither and sang, his mood mournful and full of grief. He turned to the assembled ministers and said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 以北山石為槨，用紵絮斮陳，蕠漆其閒，豈可動哉！」

translations.literal: With stone from the northern mountains for the outer coffin, ramie padding chopped and packed in, hemp and lacquer in the gaps—how could it ever be disturbed!"
translations.idiomatic: With stone from the northern mountains for the outer coffin, ramie padding chopped and packed in, and hemp and lacquer filling the gaps—how could it ever be disturbed!"

sentences.zh: 左右皆曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Those to his left and right all said: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Those to his left and right all said: "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 釋之前進曰：「使其中有可欲者，雖錮南山猶有郄；

translations.literal: Shizhi stepped forward and said: "If there is anything within that might be coveted, even if the southern mountains were used to seal it, there would still be gaps;
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi stepped forward and said: "If there is anything within that might be coveted, even if the southern mountains were used to seal it, there would still be gaps;

sentences.zh: 使其中無可欲者，雖無石槨，又何戚焉！」

translations.literal: If there is nothing within that might be coveted, then even without a stone coffin, what cause for grief would there be!"
translations.idiomatic: If there is nothing within that might be coveted, then even without a stone coffin, what cause for grief would there be!"

sentences.zh: 文帝稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised his words.

sentences.zh: 其後拜釋之為廷尉。

translations.literal: After this he appointed Shizhi as Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he appointed Shizhi as the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上行出中渭橋，有一人從橋下走出，乘輿馬驚。

translations.literal: Soon after, the emperor was traveling and emerged from the Zhongwei Bridge when a man ran out from under the bridge, startling the imperial carriage horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, while the emperor was traveling across the Zhongwei Bridge, a man darted out from beneath it, startling the horses of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 於是使騎捕，屬之廷尉。

translations.literal: He then had cavalry capture him and assigned him to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his cavalry to seize the man and handed the case over to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 釋之治問。

translations.literal: Shizhi investigated and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi conducted the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 曰：「縣人來，聞蹕，匿橋下。

translations.literal: He said: "I am a man from the county who had come here. When I heard the imperial progress, I hid under the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I am a man from the county who had come here. When I heard the imperial progress, I hid under the bridge.

sentences.zh: 久之，以為行已過，即出，見乘輿車騎，即走耳。」

translations.literal: After a long while I thought the procession had already passed, so I came out. When I saw the imperial carriage and riders, I simply fled."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while I thought the procession had already passed, so I came out. When I saw the imperial carriage and riders, I simply fled."

sentences.zh: 廷尉秦當，一人犯蹕，當罰金。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice reported his judgment: one person had violated the imperial progress, and the proper penalty was a fine in gold.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice reported his judgment: one person had violated the imperial progress, and the proper penalty was a fine in gold.

sentences.zh: 文帝怒曰：「此人親驚吾馬，吾馬賴柔和，令他馬，固不敗傷我乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said angrily: "This man personally startled my horse. My horse was fortunately gentle; had it been another horse, would it not surely have thrown and injured me?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said angrily: "This man personally startled my horse. My horse was fortunately gentle; had it been another horse, would it not surely have thrown and injured me?

sentences.zh: 而廷尉乃當之罰金！」

translations.literal: Yet the Commandant of Justice judges the penalty as only a fine in gold!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Commandant of Justice judges the penalty as only a fine in gold!"

sentences.zh: 釋之曰：「法者天子所與天下公共也。

translations.literal: Shizhi said: "The law is what the Son of Heaven shares in common with all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi said: "The law is what the Son of Heaven shares in common with all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 今法如此而更重之，是法不信於民也。

translations.literal: Now the law stands thus, yet you would make the penalty heavier—this would make the law unbelievable to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now the law stands thus, yet you would make the penalty heavier—this would make the law unbelievable to the people.

sentences.zh: 且方其時，上使立誅之則已。

translations.literal: Moreover, at that moment, if Your Majesty had ordered him immediately executed, that would have been fine.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at that moment, had Your Majesty ordered his immediate execution, that would have been the end of it.

sentences.zh: 今既下廷尉，廷尉，天下之平也，一傾而天下用法皆為輕重，民安所措其手足？

translations.literal: Now that the case has been sent down to the Commandant of Justice—the Commandant of Justice is the standard of fairness for all under heaven—if it tilts once, throughout the realm the application of law will become arbitrary in severity. Where will the people place their hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the case has been sent down to the Commandant of Justice—the Commandant of Justice is the standard of fairness for all under heaven—if it tilts once, throughout the realm the application of law will become arbitrary in severity. Where will the people place their hands and feet?

sentences.zh: 唯陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, please consider this."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, please consider this."

sentences.zh: 良久，上曰：「廷尉當是也。」

translations.literal: After a long while, the emperor said: "The Commandant of Justice's judgment is correct."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, the emperor said: "The Commandant of Justice's judgment is correct."

sentences.zh: 其後有人盜高廟坐前玉環，捕得，文帝怒，下廷尉治。

translations.literal: After this, someone stole the jade ring from before the throne in the Gao Temple. He was captured, Emperor Wen was furious, and sent it down to the Commandant of Justice for handling.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, someone stole the jade ring from before the throne in the Temple of Gaozu. The thief was captured, and Emperor Wen, furious, referred the case to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 釋之案律盜宗廟服御物者為奏，奏當棄市。

translations.literal: Shizhi examined the statutes: stealing ancestral temple ritual objects is memorialized, and the memorial calls for execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi consulted the statutes: the penalty for stealing ritual objects from the ancestral temple was public execution. He submitted his memorial accordingly.

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「人之無道，乃盜先帝廟器，吾屬廷尉者，欲致之族，而君以法奏之，非吾所以共承宗廟意也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "This man is utterly without principle—he stole the vessels of my late father's temple. I entrusted the case to the Commandant of Justice because I wished to have his entire clan executed, yet you memorialize according to the law. This is not how I mean to uphold the ancestral temples together."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "This man is utterly without principle—he stole the vessels of my late father's temple. I entrusted the case to the Commandant of Justice because I wished to have his entire clan executed, yet you memorialize according to the law. This is not how I mean to uphold the ancestral temples together."

sentences.zh: 釋之免冠頓首謝曰：「法如是足也。

translations.literal: Shizhi removed his cap and bowed his head to the ground in apology, saying: "The law as it stands is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi removed his cap and bowed his head to the ground in apology, saying: "The law as it stands is sufficient.

sentences.zh: 且罪等，然以逆順為差。

translations.literal: Moreover, crimes may be equal, but there are differences according to rebelliousness and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes may be of equal weight, yet they are graded by the degree of defiance or compliance.

sentences.zh: 今盜宗廟器而族之，有如萬分之一，假令愚民取長陵一抔土，陛下何以加其法乎？」

translations.literal: Now, for stealing ancestral temple vessels, to execute his entire clan—if even one man in ten thousand did likewise, suppose foolish people took a handful of earth from Changling: how would Your Majesty apply the law to them?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, for stealing ancestral temple vessels, to execute his entire clan—if even one man in ten thousand did likewise, suppose foolish people took a handful of earth from Changling: how would Your Majesty apply the law to them?"

sentences.zh: 久之，文帝與太后言之，乃許廷尉當。

translations.literal: After a long time, Emperor Wen spoke of it with the empress dowager, and then permitted the Commandant of Justice's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, Emperor Wen discussed the matter with the Empress Dowager and finally accepted the Commandant of Justice's ruling.

sentences.zh: 是時，中尉條侯周亞夫與梁相山都侯王恬開見釋之持議平，乃結為親友。

translations.literal: At this time, the Colonel Zhou Yafu, Marquis of Tiao, and Wang Tiankai, Marquis of Shandu and chancellor of Liang, saw that Shizhi held discussions fairly, and so became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, Zhou Yafu the Marquis of Tiao, who served as Colonel of the Guard, and Wang Tiankai the Marquis of Shandu, who served as Chancellor of Liang, observed that Shizhi deliberated with impartiality, and both became his close friends.

sentences.zh: 張廷尉由此天下稱之。

translations.literal: From this Zhang the Commandant of Justice was praised throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: From this, Zhang the Commandant of Justice won the praise of the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 後文帝崩，景帝立，釋之恐，稱病。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Jing ascended, Shizhi was fearful and claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne, Shizhi grew fearful and feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 欲免去，懼大誅至；

translations.literal: He wished to resign and leave, fearing that severe punishment would come.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to resign and leave, fearing that severe punishment would come.

sentences.zh: 欲見謝，則未知何如。

translations.literal: He wished to see and apologize, but did not know how it would be received.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to seek an audience and apologize, but did not know how it would be received.

sentences.zh: 用王生計，卒見謝，景帝不過也。

translations.literal: Using Wang Sheng's plan, he finally saw and apologized, and Emperor Jing did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Sheng's counsel, he finally obtained an audience and offered his apology. Emperor Jing did not hold it against him.

sentences.zh: 王生者，善為黃老言，處士也。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng was skilled in Huang-Lao teachings, a recluse scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng was well versed in the teachings of Huang-Lao and lived as a recluse scholar.

sentences.zh: 嘗召居廷中，三公九卿盡會立，王生老人，曰「吾韤解」，顧謂張廷尉：「為我結韤！」

translations.literal: He was once summoned to attend at court. The Three Dukes and Nine Ministers were all standing assembled when Wang Sheng, being elderly, said, "My leggings have come loose," and turned to Zhang the Commandant of Justice: "Tie my leggings for me!"
translations.idiomatic: He was once summoned to attend at court. The Three Dukes and Nine Ministers were all standing assembled when Wang Sheng, being elderly, said, "My leggings have come loose," and turned to Zhang the Commandant of Justice: "Tie my leggings for me!"

sentences.zh: 釋之跪而結之。

translations.literal: Shizhi knelt and tied them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi knelt down and tied them for him.

sentences.zh: 既已，人或謂王生曰：「獨柰何廷辱張廷尉，使跪結韤？」

translations.literal: Afterward, someone said to Wang Sheng: "Why did you alone humiliate Zhang the Commandant of Justice in court, making him kneel to tie your leggings?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, someone said to Wang Sheng: "Why did you alone humiliate Zhang the Commandant of Justice in court, making him kneel to tie your leggings?"

sentences.zh: 王生曰：「吾老且賤，自度終無益於張廷尉。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng said: "I am old and of low station; I reckoned I could never be of benefit to Zhang the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng said: "I am old and of low station; I reckoned I could never be of benefit to Zhang the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 張廷尉方今天下名臣，吾故聊辱廷尉，使跪結韤，欲以重之。」

translations.literal: Zhang the Commandant of Justice is now the empire's renowned minister. I therefore deliberately humiliated the Commandant of Justice in court, making him kneel to tie my leggings, wishing thereby to enhance his standing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the Commandant of Justice is now the empire's renowned minister. I therefore deliberately humiliated the Commandant of Justice in court, making him kneel to tie my leggings, wishing thereby to enhance his standing."

sentences.zh: 諸公聞之，賢王生而重張廷尉。

translations.literal: The various lords heard of this and esteemed Wang Sheng while honoring Zhang the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the assembled lords heard this, they admired Wang Sheng and held Zhang the Commandant of Justice in even greater esteem.

sentences.zh: 張廷尉事景帝歲餘，為淮南王相，猶尚以前過也。

translations.literal: Zhang the Commandant of Justice served Emperor Jing for over a year, became chancellor to the King of Huainan, but still bore the previous offense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the Commandant of Justice served Emperor Jing for over a year before being transferred to serve as Chancellor to the King of Huainan—still bearing the taint of his earlier offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，釋之卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, Shizhi passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In time, Shizhi died.

sentences.zh: 其子曰張摯，字長公，官至大夫，免。

translations.literal: His son was named Zhang Ni, courtesy name Changgong, served as grand master, then was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhang Zhi, courtesy name Changgong. He rose to the rank of Grand Master but was then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 以不能取容當世，故終身不仕。

translations.literal: Because he could not accommodate the current age, he never served in office throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to ingratiate himself with the powers of his day, he never held office again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 馮唐者，其大父趙人。

translations.literal: Feng Tang—his grandfather was from Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tang's grandfather was a man of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 父徙代。

translations.literal: His father moved to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His father relocated to Dai.

sentences.zh: 漢興徙安陵。

translations.literal: After Han rose, he moved to Anling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was established, the family moved to Anling.

sentences.zh: 唐以孝著，為中郎署長，事文帝。

translations.literal: Tang was renowned for filial piety and became captain of the mounted attendants, serving Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was renowned for his filial piety and served as Captain of the Attendants under Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 文帝輦過，問唐曰：「父老何自為郎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen passed by in his carriage and asked Tang: "Elder, why are you yourself serving as a mounted attendant?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen passed by in his carriage and asked Tang: "Elder, why are you yourself serving as a mounted attendant?

sentences.zh: 家安在？」

translations.literal: Where is your family settled?"
translations.idiomatic: Where is your family settled?"

sentences.zh: 唐具以實對。

translations.literal: Tang answered fully and truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Tang gave a full and truthful answer.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「吾居代時，吾尚食監高袪數為我言趙將李齊之賢，戰於鉅鹿下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "When I was in Dai, my food supervisor Gao Qu often spoke to me of the worth of the Zhao general Li Qi, who fought at Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "When I was in Dai, my food supervisor Gao Qu often spoke to me of the worth of the Zhao general Li Qi, who fought at Julu.

sentences.zh: 今吾每飯，意未嘗不在鉅鹿也。

translations.literal: Now at every meal my thoughts are never far from Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Now at every meal my thoughts are never far from Julu.

sentences.zh: 父知之乎？」

translations.literal: Do you, elder, know of him?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you, elder, know of him?"

sentences.zh: 唐對曰：「尚不如廉頗、李牧之為將也。」

translations.literal: Tang replied: "He was still not the equal of Lian Po and Li Mu as generals."
translations.idiomatic: Tang replied: "He was still not the equal of Lian Po and Li Mu as generals."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何以？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How so?"

sentences.zh: 唐曰：「臣大父在趙時，為官（卒）［率］將，善李牧。

translations.literal: Tang said: "When my grandfather was in Zhao, he served as a commandery general and was on good terms with Li Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang said: "When my grandfather was in Zhao, he served as a commandery general and was on good terms with Li Mu.

sentences.zh: 臣父故為代相，善趙將李齊，知其為人也。」

translations.literal: My father formerly served as Chancellor of Dai and was on good terms with the Zhao general Li Qi; he knew the man well."
translations.idiomatic: My father formerly served as Chancellor of Dai and was on good terms with the Zhao general Li Qi; he knew the man well."

sentences.zh: 上既聞廉頗、李牧為人，良說，而搏髀曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: The emperor, having heard how Lian Po and Li Mu conducted themselves as men, was greatly pleased, and slapping his thigh said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having heard how Lian Po and Li Mu conducted themselves as men, was greatly pleased, and slapping his thigh said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾獨不得廉頗、李牧時為吾將，吾豈憂匈奴哉！」

translations.literal: If only I could have had Lian Po and Li Mu in their day as my generals, would I have had to worry about the Xiongnu!"
translations.idiomatic: If only I could have had Lian Po and Li Mu in their day as my generals, would I have had to worry about the Xiongnu!"

sentences.zh: 唐曰：「主臣！

translations.literal: Tang said: "Your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Tang said: "Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 陛下雖得廉頗、李牧，弗能用也。」

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty obtained Lian Po and Li Mu, you would not be able to employ them."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty obtained Lian Po and Li Mu, you would not be able to employ them."

sentences.zh: 上怒，起入禁中。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and rose to enter the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and rose to withdraw into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 良久，召唐讓曰：「公柰何眾辱我，獨無閒處乎？」

translations.literal: After a long while, he summoned Tang and reproached him, saying: "Sir, why did you publicly humiliate me? Have you no private occasion for such words?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, he summoned Tang and reproached him, saying: "Sir, why did you publicly humiliate me? Have you no private occasion for such words?"

sentences.zh: 唐謝曰：「鄙人不知忌諱。」

translations.literal: Tang apologized, saying: "This rustic does not know what must be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: Tang apologized, saying: "This rustic does not know what must be avoided."

sentences.zh: 當是之時，匈奴新大入朝那，殺北地都尉卬。

translations.literal: At this time, the Xiongnu had newly invaded Chaona greatly, killing the Beidi colonel Ang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the Xiongnu had just launched a major incursion into Chaona and killed the Colonel of Beidi, Ang.

sentences.zh: 上以胡寇為意，乃卒復問唐曰：「公何以知吾不能用廉頗、李牧也？」

translations.literal: The emperor was preoccupied with the barbarian raiders, and finally asked Tang again: "Sir, how do you know I could not employ Lian Po and Li Mu?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preoccupied with the barbarian raiders, and finally asked Tang again: "Sir, how do you know I could not employ Lian Po and Li Mu?"

sentences.zh: 唐對曰：「臣聞上古王者之遣將也，跪而推轂，曰閫以內者，寡人制之；

translations.literal: Tang replied: "I have heard that when the kings of high antiquity sent forth their generals, they would kneel and push the chariot wheel, saying: 'Within the border passes, I hold command;
translations.idiomatic: Tang replied: "I have heard that when the kings of high antiquity sent forth their generals, they would kneel and push the chariot wheel, saying: 'Within the border passes, I hold command;

sentences.zh: 閫以外者，將軍制之。

translations.literal: Beyond the border passes, the general holds command.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the border passes, the general holds command.

sentences.zh: 軍功爵賞皆決於外，歸而奏之。

translations.literal: Military merits and rewards are all decided externally, and upon return memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: All matters of military merit, rank, and reward were decided in the field, and only reported to the throne upon the general's return.

sentences.zh: 此非虛言也。

translations.literal: This is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: This is no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 臣大父言，李牧為趙將居邊，軍市之租皆自用饗士，賞賜決於外，不從中擾也。

translations.literal: My grandfather said that when Li Mu was Zhao general guarding the border, the army market rents he all used to feast the soldiers, rewards decided externally, not interfered with from the center.
translations.idiomatic: My grandfather said that when Li Mu served as a Zhao general guarding the border, he used all the revenues from the army market to feast his troops. Rewards and commendations were decided in the field, without interference from the capital.

sentences.zh: 委任而責成功，故李牧乃得盡其智能，遣選車千三百乘，彀騎萬三千，百金之士十萬，是以北逐單于，破東胡，滅澹林，西抑彊秦，南支韓、魏。

translations.literal: Entrusted with authority and held responsible for success, therefore Li Mu was able to exhaust his wisdom and ability, dispatching selected chariots one thousand three hundred, archer cavalry thirteen thousand, valiant warriors of a hundred gold ten thousand, thus driving the Chanyu north, breaking Donghu, destroying Danlin, suppressing strong Qin to the west, supporting Han and Wei to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with full authority and held accountable only for results, Li Mu was able to deploy his talents to the fullest. He marshaled thirteen hundred select chariots, thirteen thousand mounted archers, and a hundred thousand warriors each worth a hundred gold. With these forces he drove the Chanyu northward, shattered the Donghu, annihilated the Danlin, checked the mighty Qin to the west, and buttressed Han and Wei to the south.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，趙幾霸。

translations.literal: At that time, Zhao nearly became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Zhao very nearly achieved hegemony.

sentences.zh: 其後會趙王遷立，其母倡也。

translations.literal: Afterward, when King Qian of Zhao ascended, his mother was a singing girl.
translations.idiomatic: Later, it so happened that King Qian of Zhao came to the throne. His mother had been a singing girl.

sentences.zh: 王遷立，乃用郭開讒，卒誅李牧，令顏聚代之。

translations.literal: When King Qian ascended, he used Guo Kai slander and finally executed Li Mu, making Yan Ju replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Once King Qian took power, he heeded the slanders of Guo Kai and had Li Mu executed, replacing him with Yan Ju.

sentences.zh: 是以兵破士北，為秦所禽滅。

translations.literal: Therefore, the army was broken and soldiers fled north, captured and extinguished by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, the army was shattered and the soldiers routed, and Zhao was captured and destroyed by Qin.

sentences.zh: 今臣竊聞魏尚為雲中守，其軍市租盡以饗士卒，［出］私養錢，五日一椎牛，饗賓客軍吏舍人，是以匈奴遠避，不近雲中之塞。

translations.literal: Now I have secretly heard that Wei Shang as Yunzhong governor uses all the army market rents to feast soldiers and officers, uses private funds to provide fodder, slaughters an ox every five days to feast guests and military officers and retainers, therefore the Xiongnu avoid from afar, not approaching Yunzhong frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have heard privately that Wei Shang, as Governor of Yunzhong, devotes all the revenues from the army market to feasting his troops. He even spends his own private funds, and slaughters an ox every five days to feast his guests, officers, and retainers. Because of this, the Xiongnu keep their distance and dare not approach the Yunzhong frontier.

sentences.zh: 虜曾一入，尚率車騎擊之，所殺其眾。

translations.literal: The captives once entered, Shang led chariots and cavalry to strike them, killing great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians once made an incursion, Shang led his chariots and cavalry against them and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 夫士卒盡家人子，起田中從軍，安知尺籍伍符。

translations.literal: Soldiers are all sons of common families, rising from the fields to follow the army, how do they know scales and tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers are all sons of common families, pulled from their fields to serve in the army. How would they know the intricacies of military tallies and registers?

sentences.zh: 終日力戰，斬首捕虜，上功莫府，一言不相應，文吏以法繩之。

translations.literal: All day they exert strength in battle, beheading and capturing captives, reporting merits to the tent headquarters—one word not corresponding, the civil officials bind them with law.
translations.idiomatic: They fight with all their strength the whole day long, taking heads and capturing prisoners, then report their achievements to headquarters. Yet if a single word does not match, the civil officials bind them with the letter of the law.

sentences.zh: 其賞不行而吏奉法必用。

translations.literal: Their rewards do not go through but the officials adherence to law must be used.
translations.idiomatic: Their rewards go undelivered, while the officials' enforcement of regulations never fails.

sentences.zh: 臣愚，以為陛下法太明，賞太輕，罰太重。

translations.literal: I foolishly believe Your Majesty laws are too clear, rewards too light, punishments too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolishness, I believe Your Majesty's laws are too exacting, your rewards too stingy, and your punishments too severe.

sentences.zh: 且雲中守魏尚坐上功首虜差六級，陛下下之吏，削其爵，罰作之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yunzhong governor Wei Shang sat for reporting captured heads six levels off, Your Majesty sent him to the officials, stripped his nobility, punished him with labor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Governor of Yunzhong, Wei Shang, was convicted because his report of enemy heads taken was off by six. Your Majesty handed him over to the officials, stripped him of his rank, and sentenced him to penal labor.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，陛下雖得廉頗、李牧，弗能用也。

translations.literal: From this it follows that even if Your Majesty obtained Lian Po and Li Mu, you would not be able to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that even if Your Majesty obtained Lian Po and Li Mu, you would not be able to employ them.

sentences.zh: 臣誠愚，觸忌諱，死罪死罪！」

translations.literal: I am truly foolish and have touched on forbidden matters—death offense, death offense!"
translations.idiomatic: I am truly foolish and have spoken what should not be spoken—I deserve death, I deserve death!"

sentences.zh: 文帝說。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was delighted.

sentences.zh: 是日令馮唐持節赦魏尚，復以為雲中守，而拜唐為車騎都尉，主中尉及郡國車士。

translations.literal: That day he commanded Feng Tang to hold the imperial seal and pardon Wei Shang, restoring him as Yunzhong governor, and appointed Tang as Chariot and Cavalry Colonel, overseeing the Colonel of the Guard and the chariot soldiers of commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: That very day, the emperor ordered Feng Tang to carry the imperial tally and pardon Wei Shang, restoring him as Governor of Yunzhong. He also appointed Tang as Chariot and Cavalry Colonel, with authority over the Colonel of the Guard and the chariot soldiers of the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 七年，景帝立，以唐為楚相，免。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Jing ascended the throne, made Tang Chancellor of Chu, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Emperor Jing ascended the throne, appointed Tang Chancellor of Chu, and later dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 武帝立，求賢良，舉馮唐。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ascended, sought worthy and good officials, recommended Feng Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne and sought out men of worth, Feng Tang was recommended.

sentences.zh: 唐時年九十餘，不能復為官，乃以唐子馮遂為郎。

translations.literal: Tang at that time was over ninety years old, could no longer serve as official, so made Tang son Feng Sui a mounted attendant.
translations.idiomatic: By that time, Tang was over ninety years old and could no longer serve. His son Feng Sui was appointed as a mounted attendant in his stead.

sentences.zh: 遂字王孫，亦奇士，與余善。

translations.literal: Sui courtesy name Wangsun, also an extraordinary gentleman, befriended me well.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, courtesy name Wangsun, was also a remarkable man, and he and I became good friends.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：張季之言長者，守法不阿意；

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: In Zhang Ji's remarks on what makes a true elder, he upholds the law without currying favor;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: In Zhang Ji's remarks on what makes a true elder, he upholds the law without currying favor;

sentences.zh: 馮公之論將率，有味哉！

translations.literal: In Lord Feng's discourse on generals and commanders—how full of meaning!
translations.idiomatic: In Lord Feng's discourse on generals and commanders—how full of meaning!

sentences.zh: 有味哉！

translations.literal: How full of meaning!
translations.idiomatic: How full of meaning!

sentences.zh: 語曰「不知其人，視其友」。

translations.literal: The saying goes, "If you do not know a man, look at his friends."
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "If you do not know a man, look at his friends."

sentences.zh: 二君之所稱誦，可著廊廟。

translations.literal: What these two gentlemen praised and recited can be recorded in the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: What these two gentlemen praised and advocated was worthy of the halls of court.

sentences.zh: 書曰「不偏不黨，王道蕩蕩；

translations.literal: The Book says, "Without partiality and without faction, the way of the king is vast and all-embracing;
translations.idiomatic: The Book says, "Without partiality and without faction, the way of the king is vast and all-embracing;

sentences.zh: 不黨不偏，王道便便」。

translations.literal: without faction and without partiality, the way of the king is level and plain."
translations.idiomatic: without faction and without partiality, the way of the king is level and plain."

sentences.zh: 張季、馮公近之矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji and Feng Gong approach it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji and Lord Feng came close to embodying this ideal.
